data.narrative:
SpectralX is a Series A defense and security company founded by Asaf Picciotto and former IDF special-forces veterans. The peer universe consists of 11 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: 2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Castelion. Five sampled peers—Dream Security ($3.0B, Series B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B, Series B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B, Series B), Code Metal ($1.2B, Series B), and Twenty ($1.0B, Series B)—illustrate the range of late-stage valuations in this sector.

The peer-median method, the primary applicable triangulation approach, yields $1.0B. This figure reflects the median valuation across the 11-company peer set, with observed valuations spanning $125M to $3.0B. No revenue multiples, discounted cash flow, or precedent transaction data were available to support alternative methods, limiting triangulation to a single valuation signal.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $850M to $1.1B, centered on $1.0B. This estimate carries material uncertainty: the single-method approach lacks corroborating signals, the peer set includes several Series B companies (later stage than SpectralX's current Series A position), and the wide peer range ($125M–$3.0B) reflects substantial heterogeneity in the defense-tech sector. Investor conviction in this range should be anchored to SpectralX's specific operational metrics, customer traction, and technical differentiation relative to named peers.
